tip: For body parts Swedish uses the definite form, not a possessive: ansiktet (the face) means my face when the owner is obvious.
Swedish says i telefon (in the phone) for on the phone, using i where English uses on.
lära sig means to learn; lära without sig means to teach. Here lärt sig marks learning, not teaching.
Use mitt (not min) before ett-words: fel is an ett-word, so it is mitt fel, my fault.
To want a thing, Swedish says vill ha (will have), not vill alone: vill ha means want to have.
sina means one's own and points back to the subject: sina ögon are his own eyes, not someone else's.
tycka om means to like, and it splits: inte lands between the two parts, tyckte inte om.
In an om (if) clause, inte comes before the verb: om du inte vill, not om du vill inte.
Start with a time phrase and the verb still comes second: Nästa vecka börjar puts börjar before the subject.
på landet means in the countryside, not on the land; landet here is rural areas, not a nation.
No article before a profession after som: jobbat som läkare, worked as a doctor, drops the a.
varandra means each other, the reciprocal pronoun: känt varandra is have known each other.
